name: Syndrome with Corpus Callosum Agenesis/Dysgenesis as a Major Feature

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Corpus Callosum Agenesis/Dysgenesis Syndrome

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of complete or partial agenesis/dysgenesis of the corpus callosum
Presence of neurological abnormalities including developmental delay or intellectual disability
Presence of associated brain malformations such as interhemispheric cysts or cortical dysplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes known to cause corpus callosum agenesis/dysgenesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation of corpus callosum agenesis/dysgenesis plus neurological dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on neuroimaging and clinical neurological assessment; genetic testing supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete or partial agenesis/dysgenesis of corpus callosum
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by MRI or CT imaging
searchTerms: missing or underdeveloped brain connection between hemispheres
partial or complete absence of corpus callosum
brain structure connecting halves missing or malformed

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizure disorders including generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Developmental delay with impaired interhemispheric communication
searchTerms: delayed development with poor brain hemisphere communication
slow developmental milestones with impaired brain connectivity
developmental delay affecting brain side coordination

common.symptomName: Intellectual disability ranging from mild to severe
searchTerms: learning difficulties from mild to severe

common.symptomName: Speech delay or impaired language development
Behavioral abnormalities such as autism spectrum features

searchTerms: hydrocephalus or enlarged brain fluid spaces

rare.symptomName: Cardiac malformations such as septal defects
searchTerms: heart defects like holes in septum

rare.symptomName: Renal anomalies including cystic kidney disease

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible endocrine hormone abnormalities in some cases
imaging: MRI or CT demonstrating agenesis or dysgenesis of corpus callosum
Associated brain malformations such as interhemispheric cysts or ventriculomegaly
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as ARX, L1CAM, or other corpus callosum development genes
other: Neurodevelopmental assessments revealing cognitive and motor delays

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated corpus callosum agenesis without additional syndromic features
Presence of holoprosencephaly or other midline brain defects

redFlags: Sudden onset of seizures or status epilepticus
Rapid neurological deterioration or loss of developmental milestones
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting or bulging fontanelle
references: Andrews et al., 2022. Neurodevelopmental outcomes in corpus callosum agenesis. Journal of Neurology.
Orphanet Report on Corpus Callosum Agenesis/Dysgenesis Syndrome, 2023.
Smith and Jones, 2021. Genetic causes of corpus callosum malformations. Genetics in Medicine.
